clue.text: Vessel going south to Uttar Pradesh?

parts.note: taken as written
UP is the abbreviation for the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh

explanation.surface: A ship sailing south towards the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a basin for holy water in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoup is a basin or drinking container, a kind of receptacle.

clue.text: Sweetener for little bag with tea in

parts.note: a sac is a small bag or pouch
char is a British slang word for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small bag of sweetener with tea inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sugar substitute.

clue.text: Cry of pain boy admitted

parts.note: ow is what someone cries when hurt
Ned is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy was let in, crying out in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a fault is to confess it, so owned means confessed.

clue.text: Disney's dog-cart adapted for a wealthy ruler

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons

indicators.note: adapted means changed in form, so the letters of cart are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog-cart from Disney, modified for a rich monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog-cart' looks like one thing, a light horse carriage, but the hyphen hides a break between the dog and the cart; 'adapted' scrambles only the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is someone who holds power because of their riches.

clue.text: Jacobson has Nathan beheaded! It's monstrous!

parts.note: Levi was one of the sons of Jacob in the Bible

indicators.note: a word beheaded loses its first letter, here the name Nathan

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a man called Jacobson has decapitated a man named Nathan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacobson' reads as a surname but means a son of Jacob; 'beheaded' turns NATHAN into ATHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is a huge sea monster of the Bible, so the word names something monstrous.

clue.text: Form of grid with modified tail, etc

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters of tail and etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grid design with an altered tail and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a crisscross framework of strips, a grid pattern.

clue.text: A composer has little weight in this decision

parts.note: Verdi was an Italian opera composer
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a small unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: A composer contributes very little to this ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little weight' looks like 'small influence' but means the abbreviated carat.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the judgment reached by a jury or judge.

clue.text: This side in Cumbria for an easy stroll?

indicators.note: this stands for the answer itself, which with side added makes the Cumbrian town, so side is removed from the town's name

parts.note: Ambleside is a town in Cumbria, in England's Lake District

explanation.surface: Somewhere on this side of Cumbria suited to a gentle walk.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'This + side' as a place in Cumbria: AMBLESIDE, a Lake District town, so 'This' is AMBLESIDE without SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amble is a leisurely walk at an easy pace.

clue.text: Suspended a heretic, one from Debrecen perhaps

parts.note: hung means suspended
an Arian followed Arius, whose teaching was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A heretic was hanged, perhaps someone from a Hungarian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Debrecen is Hungary's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Debrecen is a city in Hungary, so someone from there is an example of a native of that country.

clue.text: The old boy given a rise by the Duke of Wellington

definitions.text: The old boy given a rise by the Duke of Wellington

parts.words: The old boy given a rise by the Duke of Wellington
parts.note: 'a rise' hints at the prominent feature on his face

explanation.surface: An old chap got a pay rise from the Duke of Wellington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a rise' looks like a pay rise, but the rise is the Duke's big nose, which earned him his soldiers' nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the second half of the Duke's army nickname, earned by his prominent beak.

clue.text: Wood, in former times, for this rail?

definitions.text: Wood, in former times, for this rail?

parts.words: Wood, in former times, for this rail?
parts.note: three senses of one job title: Sir Henry Wood led the Proms orchestra, a bus or tram once had someone taking fares, and an electrified live rail carries current

explanation.surface: A question about timber once used to make a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like timber but is the conductor Sir Henry Wood, founder of the Proms; the bus ticket-collector belongs to 'former times'; a conductor rail carries electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers an orchestra leader, a fare collector and a material or rail that carries current.

clue.text: Share of profits Pompey recognized as good

definitions.meaning: an extra payment from a firm's earnings to staff or shareholders
Pompey, a Roman general, spoke Latin, in which this word means good

explanation.surface: Pompey (Portsmouth) is pleased with its slice of the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: Pompey is also the nickname of Portsmouth, which helps the business-page surface; here it is the Roman general who would know the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra payment from profits; and the Latin adjective meaning good, which a Roman would understand.

clue.text: Hotel or house, uncommonly dry inside

indicators.note: inside means the rearranged letters go within the abbreviation for house
uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters of dry are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel or house where it is unusually dry indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' looks like part of a list with 'house', but it is the definition: a hydro is a spa hotel. 'uncommonly' scrambles the dry, and 'inside' places it in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydro is a spa hotel offering water cures, so it is a kind of hotel.

clue.text: Way to go? One can take a long time by railway

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a tin is a can
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Anyone can take a long time travelling by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb but is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned route for a journey, a list of where one will travel.

clue.text: Venerate? Not quite. That is a waking dream

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: to venerate is to revere
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether venerate is the right word and decides it is not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims REVERE to REVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, a state of musing while awake.

clue.text: True novel distressed the non-conscript

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or worn, so the letters of true novel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A truthful novel upset the man who was not called up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a book but is part of the letters 'distressed' scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: A volunteer joins the forces of their own free will rather than being drafted.

clue.text: Social insect — call it oriental

parts.note: to term something is to call it
taken as written
E for East, so oriental gives E

explanation.surface: Advice to name some social insect as coming from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites live in large organised colonies, which is what makes them social insects.

clue.text: Spectacle produced by Gunner Rees? In what way?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners
taken as written
how asks in what way

explanation.surface: A show staged by an artilleryman named Rees, with someone asking how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunner Rees' looks like a soldier's rank and name, but the rank is the regiment, the Royal Artillery, and the question supplies the last part.
explanation.definitionFit: A raree-show is a peep show or street spectacle carried in a box.

clue.text: For example, boy's concealing evidence of debt! Shocking!

indicators.note: concealing means the boy's name wraps around and hides the next piece

parts.note: Reg is a boy's name, and the possessive gives REGS
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A boy is caught hiding proof of what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' tells you the boy's name wraps around the debt note; the example abbreviation comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, appalling.

clue.text: Like Mrs Malaprop's allegory — nothing relating to the ear

parts.note: nil means nothing
otic is the adjective relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A comment on Mrs Malaprop's verbal blunders that nothing to do with hearing is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Malaprop, in Sheridan's play The Rivals, says 'as headstrong as an allegory on the banks of the Nile', meaning an alligator; so her allegory is of the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic means of or belonging to the River Nile, where her 'allegory' (alligator) lives.

clue.text: Man permitted to make a wreath.

parts.note: a chap is a man
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A man is allowed to make a garland.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or circlet of flowers for the head.

clue.text: County officer, or one held by King Charles

indicators.note: held by means the following pieces sit inside the royal initials

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A county official, or someone kept in custody by King Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts the two words inside the king's initials, Carolus Rex being Latin for King Charles. 'or' looks like a link word but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is an official who investigates sudden deaths within a county or district.

clue.text: Food purveyor in motor vehicle damaged tree

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters of tree are rearranged

explanation.surface: A food supplier in a car hit a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' scrambles the tree to ATERE, and 'in' places that within the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink for events.

clue.text: Repair? Impossible for me, being a beggar

parts.note: to mend is to repair
someone saying a thing is impossible for them says I can't

explanation.surface: Someone asked to mend something says it is beyond them, being a beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is someone who lives by begging, especially a friar of a begging order.

clue.text: The marriage game

definitions.meaning: a union of two people is a good pairing

explanation.definitionFit: A match is both a wedding pairing and a sporting fixture.

clue.text: One Chateaubriand identified with peace

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
François-René de Chateaubriand wrote the novella René, and René was also his own name

explanation.surface: A single Chateaubriand steak said to be linked with peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chateaubriand' suggests the steak, but it is the French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene was the Greek goddess of peace, and the name comes from the Greek for peace.

clue.text: Balthazar (in the carol) thus stretching out his resources

parts.note: the carol We Three Kings calls them kings of Orient, that is from the East, giving E
Balthazar is traditionally one of the three kings, or Magi

explanation.surface: Balthazar, one of the Magi in the carol, makes his gifts last.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'We Three Kings of Orient Are' Balthazar is an eastern king, an E KING; 'thus' links that to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eking out supplies means making them last longer by using them sparingly.

clue.text: Bury some vain 15

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the word vain followed by the answer to 15 across, the social insect

explanation.surface: Bury some vain insects.
explanation.walkthrough: Write out 'vain' followed by the answer to 15 across, and the run straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter someone is to put them in a grave.

clue.text: Subject of article by present compiler

parts.note: the is the definite article
the setter of this puzzle refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The topic of a piece of writing by the crossword setter here present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present compiler' is the setter speaking of themselves, so ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or main idea of a work.

clue.text: Moving slowly to household gods' segregated area?

parts.note: the Lares were Roman household gods; a single one is a Lar
a ghetto is an area where a group is segregated

explanation.surface: A trip to a walled-off quarter belonging to the household gods.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural Lares has the singular LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is a musical direction for a rather slow tempo, a little faster than largo.

clue.text: A farm-worker made her starve

indicators.note: made here means formed into something new, so the letters of her starve are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmhand caused a woman to go hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals rearranging HER STARVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvester gathers in crops, so it is someone employed on a farm (or a machine doing the job).

clue.text: Such burrowers one's diet in the Rhineland Palatinate?

definitions.meaning: earth-dwelling creatures that tunnel through soil

definitions.text: one's diet in the Rhineland Palatinate?
definitions.meaning: the Diet of ... was the 1521 imperial assembly held in that German city

explanation.surface: Asks what burrowing creatures eat in a German region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' suggests food but is the Diet of Worms, the assembly that tried Martin Luther.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms burrow through soil; and Worms is a city in Rhineland-Palatinate that hosted a famous imperial Diet.
